summary: Backend-only testing of iteration-2 features: object-storage-backed file upload/view + transaction items[] + dashboard by_item aggregation. Wrote new pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_finance_features.py (8 tests). All 29 tests (21 regression + 8 new) PASS against the HTTPS ingress.

minor.issue: Returns 200 (not 201) on successful create — minor REST convention mismatch.
Accepts a JWT via query string (?auth=...) to support direct /
No filetype/MIME allow-list. Anything up to 10MB can be uploaded (e.g. executables, html). Recommend whitelist (pdf/png/jpg/jpeg/txt) and content-type sniff.
No ownership/RBAC check — any authenticated user (including viewers) can fetch any uploaded file path. Consider scoping by uploader or by linked transaction visibility.

items[] and attachments[] are part of the same body — there is no dedicated /api/transactions/{id}/attachments endpoint. PUT requires full TransactionIn replacement to add/remove attachments, which is heavy.
Uses a blocking `requests` call inside an async FastAPI route — blocks the event loop on cold start. Acceptable for low traffic; recommend httpx.AsyncClient for higher concurrency.
File metadata is stored in db.files but there is no index/uniqueness on `path`. Concurrent uploads could collide if UUID gen is identical (vanishingly small probability, but no constraint).

action_items: Consider RBAC/ownership check on /api/files/view — currently any authenticated user (incl. viewers) can read any file path.
Avoid passing JWT via ?auth= query param (leaks to logs/history); use short-lived signed URLs or one-time view tokens.
Add MIME/extension allow-list on /api/files/upload (currently any file <=10MB is accepted).
Convert blocking `requests` calls in storage helpers to async (httpx.AsyncClient) to avoid blocking FastAPI event loop.
critical_code_review_comments: /api/files/view is missing authorization — any logged-in user can read any uploaded file by path (no link to transaction visibility or uploader).
JWT-in-query (?auth=...) is a security smell: tokens land in server access logs, browser history, and Referer headers. Use a server-minted short-lived view token bound to a single object path.
_put_object/_get_object use sync `requests` inside async endpoints; blocks event loop. Use httpx.AsyncClient or run in a threadpool.
No allow-list on upload content_type or extension; an admin/manager could upload arbitrary content (e.g. .html) and serve it back via /files/view.
TransactionItem.amount is independent of quantity*rate — the backend doesn't validate consistency. Acceptable if intentional (discount etc.) but worth a comment.
_items_breakdown groups by case-sensitive item name (e.g. 'Widget' vs 'widget' are separate). Consider normalizing case before grouping for better UX.
seed_data_creation: Each pytest run creates ~3 transactions in March 2026 with a unique 'Widget_<uuid>' item name plus a few TEST_-prefixed entities. Item name is randomized per-run to keep dashboard aggregation deterministic across repeated runs. No cleanup performed (matches iteration 1 convention).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two pytest files under /app/backend/tests/: test_finance_api.py (iteration-1 regression, 21 tests) and test_finance_features.py (iteration-2 features, 8 tests). Both auto-read REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env. Override with FINANCE_TEST_BASE_URL. Item aggregation test uses a per-run unique item name to avoid contamination from previous runs. EMERGENT_LLM_KEY in backend/.env is configured and Emergent Object Storage upload/fetch works end-to-end.
rca of the issue: Initial full-suite run failed test_by_item_aggregation (got 700 expected 350) because the items_txn_ids fixture created a hard-coded 'Widget' item, and a previous test run had already left 'Widget' rows in the DB — so the aggregation correctly summed all of them. Fixed by introducing a per-session unique item_tag fixture (Widget_<uuid8>) so each run aggregates only its own data. Backend behavior is correct; the test was non-isolated. After fix, 29/29 PASS.
